subtopics.name: What is a Database?
subtopics.content: A database is an organized collection of structured data, typically stored electronically in a computer system. It is designed to allow for the easy storage, retrieval, modification, and deletion of data. Databases are essential for managing large amounts of information efficiently.

videos.title: What is a Database?
videos.ai_context: Introduction to databases and why they are used.

subtopics.name: DBMS vs RDBMS
subtopics.content: A Database Management System (DBMS) is software that interacts with users and applications to manage data. A Relational Database Management System (RDBMS) is a type of DBMS based on the relational model, which stores data in structured tables. Most modern databases like MySQL and PostgreSQL are RDBMS.

videos.title: DBMS vs RDBMS Explained
videos.ai_context: Understanding the difference between general DBMS and Relational DBMS.

subtopics.name: Types of Databases (Relational vs NoSQL)
subtopics.content: Relational databases (SQL) use structured tables with predefined schemas. NoSQL databases are designed for unstructured or semi-structured data and can be document-based, key-value, or graph-based. Choosing between them depends on the data structure and scalability needs.

videos.title: SQL vs NoSQL Databases
videos.ai_context: Comparison between Relational and NoSQL databases.

subtopics.name: Tables, Rows, Columns
subtopics.content: In a relational database, data is organized into tables. A table consists of columns (fields) that define the data type and rows (records) that represent individual entries. Understanding this structure is fundamental to working with SQL.

subtopics.name: Data Types
subtopics.content: Data types define the kind of data a column can store. Common types include INT for whole numbers, VARCHAR for strings, DATE for dates, and DECIMAL for precise numbers. Correct data type selection ensures data integrity and performance.

subtopics.name: Keys: Primary Key, Foreign Key
subtopics.content: Keys are used to identify and link data. A Primary Key uniquely identifies each record in a table and cannot be null. A Foreign Key is a field in one table that refers to the Primary Key of another table, creating a relationship between them.

subtopics.name: Introduction to SQL
subtopics.content: Structured Query Language (SQL) is the standard language for communicating with relational databases. It is used to perform tasks such as querying data (SELECT), inserting records (INSERT), updating information (UPDATE), and deleting data (DELETE).
